# the contributor audit: general normal-preserving surface parity repair

Source: `candidate 9764a982661d3ddc`.
Independent second audit: `historical context (not an accepted premise)`.

Result: PASS within the stated boundary-transport scope. This is not an
OC proof and does not assert source halfspace order.

The root read the whole construction and checked the following chain.

1. The common normal reference includes every original fiber body and
   every pair-average body. Conditional masses are bounded by one;
   replacing a triple reference by this reference scales all the
   conditional inequalities by the same nonnegative density. Only
   finitely many exceptional sets are united.
2. Pair-average bodies force one common intrinsic face dimension and
   direction for all active original faces at a fixed normal. This is
   valid even for base pairs whose midpoint is not integer. Their use
   here is ordinary convex geometry, not a claim of lattice membership.
3. Within a parity class, every reassigned product pair has integer
   midpoint. Lattice completeness supplies its actual target fiber.
   The finite auxiliary bases include the transverse face offsets;
   physical levels are counted once, not once per producing pair.
4. At temporary off-support levels the sum of actual pair-average
   conditional densities is a finite measure and supplies the needed
   envelope. At support levels the actual target density replaces it.
   Density representatives are used on simultaneous full marginal
   sets, and prior output absolute continuity handles null sets with
   infinite upper density.
5. The concave support roof has a globally finite piecewise affine
   extension. Thus normal height minus that roof is an admissible
   convex-order test. It is nonpositive on the canonical hull and zero
   on the old law, forcing the repaired law back to the actual target
   support graph. This step repairs a genuine contact issue; contact is
   not presumed to survive reassignment.
6. The final coupling constraints are imposed in physical coordinates.
   The compact Borel assembly theorem therefore requires no measurable
   choices of auxiliary tangent coordinates or pointwise density
   representatives. Marked reconstruction preserves conditional
   midpoint means, not individual old endpoint kernels.
7. Zero-dimensional conditional faces use atom capacities. The interval
   case uses its two actual endpoint normals and counting surface
   measure. No negative-dimensional surface measure is introduced.
8. At most 2^n parity classes give the exact bound. The complementary
   cube-base example forces all midpoint mass onto one actual fiber
   and certifies sharpness of this auxiliary constant.

The theorem applies to compatible positive fibers over a lattice-complete
finite base. It does not itself cover arbitrary singular volume defects,
decompose arbitrary barycentric branches into pairs, construct an OC
center, or turn convex order into order for halfspace indicators. Those
would be separate propositions requiring proofs.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
